name: A 96-Word Two-Row Overlap Envelope Has No Negative Ample Subfamily
statement: In the coordinate-$(0,1)$ two-row presentation of the labelled $267$-concept obstruction, with coordinate $1$ flipped, let $C=D_0\cap D_1$. Then $|C|=48$, and every ample subfamily of the $96$-word envelope $C\times Q_1$ is dismantlable ample. Consequently no ample forbidden two-layer family whose union is this labelled $C$ can be the reduced input of a two-row assembly, even when the large rows change while retaining intersection $C$.
proof: The overlap is reconstructed from the seed as the contraction in coordinate one of the reduction in coordinate zero and is directly verified ample of order $48$. An exact all-subfamily formula leaves all $96$ membership variables free, requires nonemptiness and ampleness through equality of shattered and strongly shattered supports, and requires cornerlessness through a missing vertex in each retained incident cube. The resulting formula has $3222$ variables and $21485$ clauses and an independently replayed DRAT refutation. Hence every nonempty ample subfamily has a corner; deleting corners and inducting on order proves dismantlability.
comments: The result concerns this labelled envelope and imposes no projection or cardinality cutoff. It is not a universal $96$-vertex theorem and does not resolve the two-row inverse for other intersections.
